Question: Anthony is a project manager in a software consulting organization. His project has a high level of change associated with it. There is active and ongoing stakeholder involvement. This means he is probably working with a(n):
Explanation: Projects with adaptive life cycles are intended to respond to high levels of change and require ongoing stakeholder engagement. PMBOK guide-6th-edition page 131

Question: The development life cycle type in which the deliverable is produced through a series of iterations that successively add functionality within a predetermined time frame is called:
Explanation: In an incremental life cycle, the deliverable is produced through a series of iterations that successively add functionality within a predetermined time frame. The deliverable contains the necessary and sufficient capability to be considered complete only after the final iteration. PMBOK guide-6th-edition page 19

Question: Mariam has reached the end of the design phase of a construction project. She decides to call a "phase end review" for obtaining authorization to close the design phase and initiate the next phase (i.e., execution phase) of her project. The functional manager disagrees with her suggestion. He wants a "kill point" to formally end the design phase of the project. In this context, Mariam should:
Choice 1: A) Disagree with the functional manager because she knows that phase end reviews should be used at the end of each phase of the project.
Choice 2: B) Agree with the functional manager as kill point is a phase-end review.
Choice 3: C) Escalate this issue to the project sponsor.
Choice 4: D) Take advice from a senior project manager about what should actually be done at the end of each phase of the project.
Explanation: A phase gate, is held at the end of a phase. Depending on the organization, industry, or type of work, phase gates may be referred to by other terms such as, phase review, stage gate, kill point, and phase entrance or phase exit. PMBOK guide-6th-edition page 21

Question: Shawn works as a project manager for a construction company. His company regularly builds teams to create products for clients. When the product is delivered, the team is dissolved and assigned to other projects. What kind of organizational structure of his company?
Explanation: Table 2-1. Organizational Structure and its influences on projects, Information Technology Project Management, page 50

Question: You have just been hired to work in an ongoing project in which the functional managers are responsible for arranging work groups while the project manager is responsible for managing the project budget. What organizational structure type is being used in such project?
Explanation: Table 2-1. Organizational Structure and its influences on projects, Information Technology Project Management, page 50

Question: You have been appointed as a full-time manager for a smart watches production project. You are reporting to the functional manager of the integration track who will manage the project budget. What type of organization structure are you part of?
Explanation: The role of the project manager is mostly part time in organic and functional organization structure. Thus, A and D are not correct. In Matrix-Strong organization, the project manager is required full time, but at the same time it is generally the project manager who takes care of the budget so, C is also not correct. The roles are mixed in hybrid organization, and the above scenario is an ideal example of Hybrid organization structure. Consequently, among all choices provided B is the best answer. PMBOK guide-6th-edition page 47

Question: Your team members told you that they are overloaded with many tasks. They are saying that they have many tasks assigned to them besides the main tasks in the project. You promised them that you would clear the overloaded tasks. You are a project manager in:
Explanation: It is clear that the project manager has full power to remove the overloaded tasks from team members, and because team members have many tasks besides the main tasks in the project so, it is a strong organization.

Question: William is managing a manufacturing project. His project team members have a dual reporting structure: they report to him and also to the functional manager. The project team members are expecting to do the project work in addition to the department work. Which form of organization is William working in?
Explanation: Matrix Organization. Any organizational structure in which the project manager shares responsibility with the functional managers for assigning priorities and for directing the work of persons assigned to the project. PMBOK guide-6th-edition page 710

Question: Where should the project manager obtain the initial cost-benefit analysis?
Explanation: The business case has the complete cost-benefit analysis for the project. It can provide the project manager with all the initial information used to justify the project. PMBOK 6th Edition, Page 125.

Question: The iterative process of increasing the level of detail in a project management plan as greater amounts of information and more accurate estimates become available is called:-
Explanation: Progressive Elaboration. The iterative process of increasing the level of detail in a project management plan as greater amounts of information and more accurate estimates become available. PMBOK guide-6th-edition page 715

Question: Frank has assigned multiple team leads for different tasks. He is managing the release of a new drug in the market. His role is that of a:
Choice 1: A) Functional Manager, because he has good functional knowledge of the pharmaceutical industry.
Choice 2: B) Project Manager, because he is creating a unique product within specific time schedules.
Choice 3: C) Operations Manager, because he has to do several repetitive tasks.
Choice 4: D) Program Manager, because he has to manage several projects to do his job effectively. "
Explanation: Table 2-1. Influences of Organizational Structures on Projects PMBOK guide-6th-edition page 47

Question: Which of the following is considered a review at the end of a phase in which a decision is made to continue to the next phase, to continue with modification, or to end a project or program?
Explanation: Phase Gate. A review at the end of a phase in which a decision is made to continue to the next phase, to continue with modification, or to end a project or program. PMBOK guide-6th-edition page 713

Question: Ben is the CEO of an infrastructure company. Currently, the company has acquired another software development company. In a steering committee meeting, Ben asks his senior leadership team to plan and initiate the activities related to merging of two organizations. Merging two organizations is an example for:
Explanation: Merging of two organizations is an example for Project because project is a temporary endeavor and has a start and end date. PMBOK guide-6th-edition page 5

Question: A CEO of a solar panels assembling company involves his senior leadership team to prepare a business case for authorizing a project to establish guidelines for handling dangerous materials. This business case is originated as a result of:-
Explanation: Establishment of proper guidelines periodically for handling dangerous materials is a mandatory legal need which every manufacturer needs to follow. PMBOK guide-6th-edition page 78

Question: You are working on a small internal project. The primary purpose of the project is to introduce a new product for the sales and marketing team which can help them manage their portfolio. Which one of the following statements best defines the difference between a program and portfolios in regard to scope?
Choice 1: A) Programs do not have scopes because they are made up of projects. Portfolios have an organizational scope.
Choice 2: B) Programs have larger scopes than projects. Portfolios have an organizational scope.
Choice 3: C) Programs have larger scopes than projects. Portfolios don’t have scopes because they are a financial investment.
Choice 4: D) Programs and portfolios can share the same scope because a portfolio may have two or more programs.
Explanation: Table 1-2. Comparative Overview of Portfolios, Programs, and Projects PMBOK guide-6th-edition page 13

Question: Which of the following is NOT considered a type of organizational structure?
Explanation: There is nothing called Matrix-Hybrid.

Question: All the following are external Enterprise Environmental Factors (EEFs) except:
Explanation: EEFs vary widely in type or nature. These factors need to be considered if the project is to be effective. EEFs include but are not limited to the factors described in Sections 2.2.1 and 2.2.2. PMBOK guide-6th-edition pages 38, 39.

Question: You are managing an infrastructure project. The completion date for a critical milestone is approaching, but a shared team is unable to commit to achieving it on schedule. What should you do to meet the milestone date?
Choice 1: A) Ask the client to change the milestone date.
Choice 2: B) Remind the shared team about the importance of the milestone.
Choice 4: D) Approach the shared team's functional manager to request additional support.
Explanation: The project manager is working in a matrix or functional organization so, the project manager should approach the shared team's functional manager to request additional support. Option (Remind the shared team about the milestone's importance) is not a good action because they are already unable to commit to achieving it on schedule. Option (Request the additional resources) is not correct because the project manager has no authority and should ask the functional manager for support. Option (Ask the client to change the milestone date) is not a good practice in such situation.

Question: The customer asks the project manager to share the latest work performance report in WhatsApp; as he is out for vacation. What should the project manager do next?
Choice 1: A) Review organization process assets to know policies and procedures.
Choice 2: B) Discuss the issue with team and senior management.
Choice 3: C) Immediately share the report to the customer.
Choice 4: D) Politely refuse to share the report in WhatsApp; as it is unethical.
Explanation: Here in this scenario, the project manager should first review the organization process assets (OPA) to know the corporate policies and procedures for social media, ethics, and security. PMBOK guide-6th-edition page 383

Question: Roy works as a project manager for a construction company. He has recently joined the organization and has been given a very large and complex project. Where can Roy expect software, templates, and standardized policies?
Explanation: Processes, policies, and procedures are usually established by the project management office (PMO) or another function outside of the project. These can be updated only by following the appropriate organizational policies associated with updating processes, policies, or procedures. PMBOK guide-6th-edition page 40

Question: Antonio is a project manager who is working with the project team to prepare project management plan. The project requires at least 5 resources who have specialized knowledge on a particular niche technology. What needs to be reviewed to find out whether such resources are available internally?
Explanation: Resource availability and employee capability are examples of internal EEF. Project team should review internal EEF to get the information in relation to resource and knowledge available internally within the organization. PMBOK guide-6th-edition page 38

Question: One of the most important tools and techniques a project manager should have while managing a team is the interpersonal and team skills such as:
Explanation: Figure 9-12. Manage Team: Inputs, Tools & Techniques, and Outputs PMBOK guide-6th-edition page 345.

Question: Mindy is a senior project manager who is presently performing Define Scope, Define Activities, Develop Schedule, and Determine Budget processes. These responsibilities are performed as part of:
Explanation: Planning Process Group. Those processes required to establish the scope of the project, refine the objectives, and define the course of action required to attain the objectives that the project was undertaken to achieve. PMBOK guide-6th-edition page 23

Question: The project of building a new sports stadium is running smoothly with a team of generalizing specialists. The control of the product planning and delivery has been delegated to the project team. The project manager is trying to build a collaborative decision-making environment while ensuring that the team has the ability to respond to changes. What development approach is being followed in this project?
Explanation: Agile projects run in iterative and incremental fashion with team responsible for planning and delivery. The question suggests that the project is being run using Agile approach where team is controlling planning and execution. PMBOK guide-6th-edition page 74

Question: You are managing a project which has developers, quality specialists and HR professionals. You have maximum authority. To which organizational structure does your company belong?
Explanation: Table 2-1. Organizational Structure and its influences on projects, Information Technology Project Management, page 50

Question: Several experts have gathered to build an implementation strategy for making a data protection software for a new IT organization. What can guide them with information in relation to legal and regulatory requirements and constraints to be taken care while developing a document that will formally authorize the existence of the project?
Choice 3: C) Historical Information in relation to Data Protection
Explanation: In this case, EEF needs to be reviewed to take necessary guidance on legal and regulatory requirements which can impact the upcoming project in future. Further, EEF is an input for develop project charter process, and currently develop project charter process is getting performed. PMBOK guide-6th-edition page 78

Question: Marcos is a leader of a contracting company. He is heading a department that standardizes project related governance processes and acts as liaison between the balanced scorecard and the program, projects, portfolios of the organization. He has high degree of authority, and the project managers of all business critical projects are reporting to him. What kind of organization structure type Marcos is leading?
Choice 1: A) Marcos is acting as the COO of the contracting company.
Choice 2: B) Marcos is heading a strong matrix organization.
Choice 3: C) Marcos is heading a PMO of type Controlling.
Choice 4: D) Marcos is heading a PMO of type Directive.
Explanation: The question states that Marcos is leading project management office of the contracting company. There are three types of PMO:- Supportive, Directive, and Controlling. According to the situation stated in the question, Marcos is heading PMO of type Directive. Directive PMOs control and manage the project, and project managers directly report to the PMO. PMBOK guide-6th-edition page 48

Question: You have recently joined a trading company as a project manager. The senior management has involved you in the preparation of the project charter for their car tyres manufacturing project. What should you do to know the marketplace conditions and current industry standards?
Choice 2: B) Review the enterprise environmental factors (EEF) internal to the organization.
Choice 3: C) Review the enterprise environmental factors (EEF) external to the organization.
Choice 4: D) Examine the historical information and lessons learned repository.
Explanation: The question states that the recently joined project manager has been involved in the preparation of the project charter of the company’s upcoming internal project. Here, all options are inputs to the develop project charter process, but the question asked what needs to be reviewed to know the market conditions and industry standards, which are examples of external enterprise environmental factors, because they are outside the control of the project team. Therefore, among all options provided, C is the best answer. PMBOK guide-6th-edition pages 39, 78

Question: A collection of related projects that are managed in a coordinated way to obtain benefits is called a:
Explanation: The PMBOK Guide defines a Program as: "a group of related projects, subsidiary programs, and program activities managed in a coordinated manner to obtain benefits not available from managing them individually".

Question: You are working for an organization which heavily follows the PMI processes and methodologies. Your colleagues often talk about the enterprise environmental factors. Which of the following statements about Enterprise Environmental Factors is NOT true?
Choice 1: A) Neither promote nor hold back the project management processes.
Choice 2: B) May restrict the project management processes.
Choice 3: C) May promote the project management processes.
Choice 4: D) May either promote or hold back the project management processes.
Explanation: Enterprise environmental factors (EEFs) refer to conditions, not under the control of the project team, that influence, constrain, or direct the project. These conditions can be internal and/or external to the organization. EEFs are considered as inputs to many project management processes, specifically for most planning processes. These factors may enhance or constrain project management options. In addition, these factors may have a positive or negative influence on the outcome. PMBOK guide-6th-edition page 38
